cnd20:1.3: my eyes are not clear, my hearing is poor;
cnd20:1.5: Explain the teaching so that I may understand;
cnd20:2.2: I am old: old, elderly, senior, advanced in years, having reached the final stage of life, a hundred and twenty years old from birth.
cnd20:2.3: Feeble: weak, of little strength, of little stamina.
cnd20:2.4: Pallid: with faded color, with color gone, with color departed.
cnd20:2.5: That former beauty, the glow of complexion, has vanished, and the drawbacks have become manifest—
cnd20:3.4: Piṅgiya: this is the name of that brahmin … expression—
cnd20:4.1: My eyes are not clear, my hearing is poor: the eyes are not clear, not very clear, not completely clear, not bright.
cnd20:4.4: My hearing is poor: the ear is not clear, not very clear, not completely clear, not bright.
cnd20:5.2: Let me not perish: let me not perish, let me not be destroyed, let me not be utterly lost.
cnd20:5.3: Confused: confused by delusion, fallen into ignorance, unknowing, undiscerning, of poor wisdom.
cnd20:5.4: Midway: without having understood, attained, known, gained, touched, or realized your teaching, view, practice, and path, I might die right in the middle—
cnd20:6.1: Explain the teaching so that I may understand.
cnd20:6.2: The teaching: the spiritual practice that’s good in the beginning, good in the middle, and good in the end, meaningful and well-phrased, entirely full and pure; the four kinds of mindfulness meditation, the four right efforts, the four bases of psychic power, the five faculties, the five powers, the seven awakening factors, the noble eightfold path, extinguishment and the practice that leads to extinguishment: explain, teach, assert, establish, clarify, analyze, disclose, and reveal—
cnd20:6.4: So that I may understand: so that I might know, understand, discern, comprehend, penetrate, attain, touch, and realize—
cnd20:7.1: The giving up of rebirth and old age here: right here, the giving up, stilling, letting go, and calming of rebirth, old age, and death, which is the deathless, extinguishment—
cnd20:10.2: Form: the four primary elements, and form derived from the four primary elements.
cnd20:10.3: Beings, because of form, owing to form, on account of form, are struck, harmed, hurt, and injured.
cnd20:10.5: They flog with whips, they flog with canes, they flog with clubs; they cut off hands, they cut off feet, they cut off hands and feet; they cut off ears, they cut off noses, they cut off ears and noses; they apply the porridge pot, the shell-shave, Rāhu’s mouth, the garland of fire, the burning hand, the bulrush twist, the bark dress, the antelope, the meat hook, the coins, the caustic pickle, the twisting bar, the straw mat; they splash them with hot oil, they have them eaten by dogs, they impale them alive on stakes, and they behead them with swords.
cnd20:10.6: In this way, beings, because of form, owing to form, on account of form, are struck, harmed, hurt, and injured.
cnd20:10.7: Having seen and observed beings being struck, harmed, hurt, and injured in this way, and having weighed it up, judged it, clarified it, and made it manifest—
cnd20:11.2: Piṅgiya: the Blessed One addresses that brahmin by name.
cnd20:11.3: Blessed One: this is a term of respect … a designation arising from realization, namely, Blessed One—
cnd20:12.2: Afflicted: they are afflicted, disturbed, oppressed, and chafed; they become sick and sad.
cnd20:12.3: By eye disease they are afflicted, disturbed, oppressed, and chafed; they become sick and sad.
cnd20:12.6: By the touch of flies, mosquitoes, wind, sun, and reptiles, they are afflicted, disturbed, oppressed, and chafed; they become sick and sad—
cnd20:13.1: Or else, when the eye is declining, diminishing, deteriorating, shrinking, passing away, and disappearing, they are afflicted …
cnd20:13.22: When medicines and supplies for the sick are declining, diminishing, deteriorating, shrinking, passing away, and disappearing, they are afflicted, disturbed, oppressed, and chafed; they become sick and sad—
cnd20:14.1: Folk: aristocrats, brahmins, peasants, and menials; laypeople and renunciates; gods and humans.
cnd20:14.2: Negligent: negligence is to be spoken of in terms of bad conduct by way of body, speech, or mind; abandoning the mind to the five kinds of sensual stimulation, and persisting in that abandonment; and, in developing skillful qualities, acting without care, acting without persistence, acting without steadiness, sluggish behavior, giving up enthusiasm, giving up responsibility, not practicing, not developing, not cultivating, not resolving, not committing oneself: this is negligence.
cnd20:14.3: Whatever negligence of this kind there is, the act of being negligent, the state of having been negligent—
cnd20:14.5: Folk who are endowed with this negligence are negligent—
cnd20:15.2: Therefore: for that reason, for that cause, owing to that condition, from that source, seeing the drawback in forms in this way—
cnd20:15.4: Diligent: acting carefully, acting persistently … diligence regarding skillful qualities—
cnd20:16.2: Form: the four primary elements, and form derived from the four primary elements.
cnd20:16.3: Give up form: let go of form, abandon form, dispel form, eliminate form, obliterate form.
cnd20:16.4: So as not to be reborn: so that your form would cease right here, and a state of existence with a fresh conception would not arise in the sensual realm, the realm of form, or the formless realm; in sensual existence, form existence, or formless existence; in percipient existence, non-percipient existence, or neither-percipient-nor-non-percipient existence; in one-constituent existence, four-constituent existence, or five-constituent existence; it would not be generated, produced, born, or reborn again in any destination, rebirth, conception, state of existence, transmigration, or cycle; it would cease right here, be stilled, come to an end, and subside—
cnd20:18.3: Nothing is unseen by you, unheard, or unthought,
cnd20:18.4: nor is anything at all unknown in the world;
cnd20:18.5: Explain the teaching so that I may understand,
cnd20:19.1: The four quarters, the four intermediate directions, below and above, these ten directions: that means the ten directions.
cnd20:20.1: Nothing is unseen by you, unheard, or unthought, nor is anything at all unknown in the world: for you there is nothing at all unseen, unheard, unthought, or unknown—whether a matter of one’s own good, the good of others, or the good of both; a matter of benefit in this life or in the next; a matter that is plain, deep, hidden, concealed, implicit, explicit, blameless, free of defilements, purified, or ultimate—there is none, it doesn’t exist, it isn’t found, it can’t be obtained—
cnd20:20.2: Nothing is unseen by you, unheard, or unthought, nor is anything at all unknown in the world.
cnd20:21.1: Explain the teaching so that I may understand.
cnd20:21.3: Explain, teach, assert, establish, clarify, analyze, disclose, and reveal extinguishment and the practice that leads to extinguishment.
cnd20:21.4: So that I may understand: so that I might know, understand, discern, comprehend, penetrate, attain, touch, and realize—
cnd20:22.1: The giving up of rebirth and old age here: right here, the giving up, stilling, letting go, and calming of rebirth, old age, and death, which is the deathless, extinguishment—
cnd20:25.2: Craving: craving for sights … craving for thoughts.
cnd20:25.3: Sunk in craving: sunk in craving, following craving, gone along with craving, spread over by craving, fallen into craving, entered into craving, overpowered, with mind taken over.
cnd20:25.5: Observing: observing, seeing, looking at, contemplating, and examining—
cnd20:25.8: Piṅgiya: the Blessed One addresses that brahmin by name.
cnd20:25.9: Blessed One: this is a term of respect … a designation arising from realization, namely, Blessed One—
cnd20:26.2: Tormented: tormented by rebirth, tormented by old age, tormented by illness, tormented by death, tormented by sorrow, lamentation, pain, sadness, and distress, tormented by the suffering of hell …
cnd20:26.3: tormented by the suffering of loss of view, beset by calamity, disaster, and misfortune—
cnd20:26.5: Mired in old age: touched by old age, beset, enveloped, and possessed by it.
cnd20:26.6: Followed by rebirth, spread over by old age, overpowered by illness, struck down by death, unprotected, unsheltered, without refuge, having become without refuge—
cnd20:27.2: Therefore: for that reason, for that cause, owing to that condition, from that source, seeing the drawback in craving in this way—
cnd20:28.2: Craving: craving for sights … craving for thoughts.
cnd20:28.3: Give up craving: let go of craving, abandon craving, dispel craving, eliminate craving, obliterate craving.
cnd20:28.5: a state of existence with a fresh conception would not arise in the sensual realm, the realm of form, or the formless realm; in sensual existence, form existence, or formless existence; in percipient existence, non-percipient existence, or neither-percipient-nor-non-percipient existence; in one-constituent existence, four-constituent existence, or five-constituent existence; it would not be generated, produced, born, or reborn again in any destination, rebirth, conception, state of existence, transmigration, or cycle; it would cease right here, be stilled, come to an end, and subside—
cnd20:30.1: As the verses came to an end, the stainless, immaculate vision of the Dhamma arose in those many thousands of beings who shared that brahmin’s wish, endeavor, intention, and conditioning—
cnd20:30.2: “Whatever is liable to arise, all that is liable to cease.”
cnd20:30.3: And in that brahmin the stainless, immaculate vision of the Dhamma arose—
cnd20:30.4: “Whatever is liable to arise, all that is liable to cease.”
cnd20:30.5: As soon as he gained the vision of the Dhamma, his antelope hide, matted hair, bark garment, triple staff, water pot, hair, and beard vanished; he sat there with shaven head, wearing an ochre robe, carrying outer robe, bowl, and robe, with joined palms, paying homage to the Blessed One by practicing in line with the meaning—
cnd20:30.6: “Sir, the Blessed One is my Teacher, and I am his disciple.”
